planning.question: Who is in your story? Give them a name.
Where does your story happen?
planning.hint: a pond by a tall tree

planning.question: How does it end?
planning.hint: an owl gives Pip a ride

lessons.title: Beginning, middle, end
lessons.idea: Every story starts, something happens, and then it ends.
lessons.after: Dot planted a seed. Dot watered it every day. At last, a tall sunflower grew!
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: give it a beginning, middle, and end.

selfCheck.prompt: Tap the page where your story begins.
selfCheck.secondPrompt: Now tap the page where your story ends.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: You gave your story a beginning on page {page}.
lessons.job: Add one more thing that happens in the middle.

lessons.title: Someone wants something
lessons.idea: A story starts moving when someone wants something.
lessons.before: Bo the bear sat by the river.
lessons.after: Bo the bear sat by the river, wishing for a big fish.
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: show what your main character wants.

selfCheck.prompt: Tap the sentence where your character wants something.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: Your character wanted something on page {page}.
lessons.job: Add why your character wants it.

lessons.title: Something gets in the way
lessons.idea: A story gets exciting when something gets in the way.
lessons.after: Tam walked to the party, but a big log blocked the path.
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: put something in your character's way.

selfCheck.prompt: Tap the sentence where something gets in the way.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: On page {page}, something got in the way. That makes it exciting!
lessons.job: Add one thing your character tries.

tip.job: Find an "and then" and start that sentence a new way.

lessons.title: Three acts
lessons.idea: A story has three acts. Trouble starts, gets bigger, then gets solved.
lessons.before: Pip lost a hat and found it.
lessons.after: Pip lost a hat. Then the wind blew it into the pond! A kind duck swam out and brought it back.
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: make the trouble grow, then solve it.
lessons.reminder: Trouble starts, gets bigger, gets solved

selfCheck.prompt: Tap the page where the trouble starts.
selfCheck.secondPrompt: Now tap the page where the trouble gets solved.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: Your trouble starts on page {page}. Readers will want to know what happens!
lessons.job: Make the trouble a little bigger before it gets solved.

tip.job: Add a page in the middle where the trouble gets bigger.

lessons.title: Use your senses
lessons.idea: Tell what things look, sound, smell, taste or feel like.
lessons.after: Lu walked into the warm kitchen. It smelled like apple pie!
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: tell what something sounds or smells like.

selfCheck.prompt: Tap a sentence with a sound, smell, look, or feel.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: Your words on page {page} help readers feel like they're there.
lessons.job: Add one detail to a page, like a sound or a smell.

lessons.title: Talking
lessons.idea: Let your characters talk. Write the words they say.
lessons.before: Nell said the cake was gone.
lessons.after: "Oh no, the cake is gone!" Nell said.
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: let a character say something.

selfCheck.prompt: Tap a sentence where someone talks.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: Someone talks on page {page}. Readers can hear your characters!

lessons.title: Show feelings
lessons.idea: Show how a character feels by what their body does.
lessons.before: Dot was scared of the storm.
lessons.after: When the thunder boomed, Dot's legs shook. Dot hid under the blanket.
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: show a feeling without saying its name.
lessons.reminder: How does your character's body show it?

selfCheck.prompt: Tap a sentence that shows a feeling.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: On page {page}, readers can tell how your character feels.
lessons.job: Show how your character feels at the end.

lessons.title: Endings that change someone
lessons.idea: By the end, your character is different. Maybe braver, kinder, or smarter.
lessons.after: Bo found the way home. Now Bo always takes a map.
lessons.tryIt: Try it in your book: show how your character changed.
lessons.reminder: How is your character different now?

selfCheck.prompt: Tap the sentence where your character changed.
selfCheck.notYetOffer: That's okay! Want to go back and add it?

lessons.praise: Your character changed on page {page}. Readers will remember that!
lessons.job: Add one sentence about what is different now.

tip.job: Try an ending where the problem really gets solved.

messages.finished: You finished your book. You're an author!
messages.noLessonYet: Tadpole is still writing the next lesson. Keep making books!
messages.pickLesson: Pick one lesson to use in this book.
